rows.author: C002
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REGULATE AND MODERNIZE THE PRACTICE OF CHEMISTRY IN THE PHILIPPINES, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 754
rows.abstract: "Chemistry Law of 2002". The proposed new Chemistry Law seeks to INTRODUCE the following important CHANGES: (1) Update the definition of the professional practice of chemistry; (2) Redefine the scope of the professional practice of chemistry; (3) Redefine the practice of the chemical technician; (4) Rationalize the relationship between chemistry and related professions.; (5) Strengthen the linkage between the training of chemists and the professional practice of chemistry; (6) Strengthen the authority of the Board of Chemistry to supervise chemistry laboratories and other entities which practice chemistry to ensure that the minimum quality standards are maintained; (7) Introduce a requirement for Continuing Professional Education (CPE) forr the continuous training of professional chemists; and (8) Bring the new law in line with the new PRC law of 2000.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2002-05-23

rows.author: D039
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXTENDING THE PRESCRIPTIVE PERIOD FOR RECTIFICATION OF SIMULATED BIRTHS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8552, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE DOMESTIC ADOPTION ACT OF 1998
rows.title_short: Extending the Prescriptive Period of Simulated Births, Amending for the Purpose RA 8552, Domestic Adoption Act
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is the fact that most \"adoptions\" in the Philippines have been and continue to be handled trough \"simulation of birth\". It is estimated that there are several hundred thousand Filipinos who have been \"informally: adopted in this manner. In these cases, because the assumed filiation under simulated births has no legal basis, the child, though no fault of its own, is deprived of the benefits and legal protection afforded by law to legally adopted children.> For this reason, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-12-17, transmitted to on 2002-12-18 and received by the Senate on 2003-01-06

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ESTABLISH A HIGHER STANDARD OF PROMOTION AND PROTECTION OF THE RIGHTS AND WELFARE OF FILIPINO OVERSEAS SEAFARERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Overseas Seafarers Act". Rationale: Today's so-called unsung heroes or modern day economic warriors have greatly contributed to our national coffers. In fact, they are the reason for our country's staying afloat in the middle of severe economic crisis.> Of this total amount, the Filipino seafarers remitted $2.3 billion to the country, posting the only increase in remittances among all overseas Filipino workers. Indeed this marginalized sector of OFWs is a vital cog in sustaining the much-needed dollar reserves of our country. > It is precisely because of the sheer number of current Filipino seafarers and the outbound student apprentices that legislative measures are considered imperative to ensure their safety, protect their rights and prromote their welfare.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PREVENT THE COLLAPSE OF THE AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES MODERNIZATION ACT (AFMA) OF 1997 BY AMENDING SECTION 112 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8435
rows.abstract: Rationale: In 1995, Congress created the Congressional Commission to review and assess the state of Philippine agriculture. This resulted, among others, in the enactment of R.A. No. 8435, otherwise known as the "Agriculture and Fishereies Modernization Act of 1997." In order to empower the agriculture and fisheries sectors to develop and sustain themselves, the amount of Twenty Billion Pesos (P20 B) was appropriated as an initial funding for the first year of the implementation of the agriculture and fisheries modernization program and an additional amount of not less than Seventeen Billion Pesos (P17 B) annually for the next six (6) years of its implementation. > However, though huge amount have been appropriated, miserable amounts were rreleased annually. In order to prevent the collpse of the Agriculture and Fisheries Modernization Act, this Bill seeks to extend the annual mandated financial support for another three (3) years. Immediate approval hereof is earnestly sought.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MANDATORY APPOINTMENT OF SOCIAL WELFARE AND DEVELOPMENT OFFICERS FOR MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Rationale: Social welfare services include activities on case work, group and community organizations. Its main goal is to assist individuals, groups and communities towards coordinated action which will ultimately lead to the improvement of their economic and social conditions. Social welfare services, indeed has, for its profession base social workers who are primarily tasked with these social services activites aimed at facilitating and strengthening the basic social relationships and the mutual adjustment between individuals and their environment for the good of society.> In view of the aforemetioned consideration, the existence oif a person to help uplift the living condition of the disadvantages sector of the society is a must, thusthe appointment of a duly licensed social workers in the municipal government should be mandatory. Hence, this bill, approval of which is sought.

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING JUNE 2 OF THE YEAR AS FIL-HISPANO DAY
rows.abstract: The State recognizes the uncommon valor and nationalism of the Spanish soldiers that laid siege in the Church of Baler from 27 June 1898 to 2 June 1899, when they surrendered to the Filipino forces, and pursuant to the decree of President Emilio Aguinaldo dated 30 June 1899 declaring them friends of the Republic of the Philippines, desires to promote better relations between our two nationa.> The Second of June of each year is hereby declared as Fil-Hispano Friendship Day to commemorate cultural historical ties, friendship and cooperation between the Philippines and Spain. It shall be a non-working holiday in Aurora Province and a working holiday in all other parts of the Philippines.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2002-05-30

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING JUNE 30 OF THE YEAR AS PHILIPPINE-SPAN ISH FRIENDSHIP DAY, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Declaring June 30 as Philippine-Spanish Friendship Day
rows.abstract: It is the policy of the State to strengthen the relationship between the Philippines and countries with which it has shared history, values and traditions. > June 30 is a day when President Emilio Aguinaldo commended the besieged Spanish soldiers inthe Church of Baler for their loyalty and gallantry. To mark this momentous occasion, there is a need to declare said day a national holiday to remember the act of benevolence which has paved the way in bridging better relations between Philippinesand Spain. > The Thirtieth of June of each year is hereby declared as Philippine-Span ish Friendship Day to commemorate cultural historical ties, friendship and cooperation between the Philippines and Spain. It shall be declared as a national speciall working holiday and a special non-working holiday in Aurora Province.
rows.status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09187) enacted on 2003-02-05

rows.title_full: AN ACT EMPOWERING WOMEN BY PROVIDING THEM WITH FINANCIAL EDUCATIONAL AND INFORMATION ASSISTANCE IN ORDER FOR THEM TO EXCEL IN COMMERCE AND TRADE
rows.abstract: "Women Empowerment in Enterprise Act." Rationale: Women in the Philippines are perceived to be more empowered than most of their counterparts in other societies and cultures. However, the empowered image of the Filipino women is flawed when one studies thier position in economic and public life. They continue to account for a higher nuumber of unemployed, wo under inhospitable conditions, receive lower pay, and are the last to be trained and the first to be laid off. They also have limited opportunities for growth in corporations, factories and other work places. In such discriminatory situations, women have to look, therefore, for other fields of endeavors where they can excel, like in entreprenuershi p, which now merges as an attractiveoption for women who want to reap the full harvest of their efforts.

This bill seeks to provide persons arrested and charged with crimes or offenses, except those involving heinous crimes, the opportunity to be released immediately without the need to post a bail bond by way of the Pre-Trial Release (PTR) Program. This bill seeks the creation of the Pre-Trial Release Office under the direct control and supervision of the Department of Justice to administer the said Program. rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING POP, ROCK OR SIMILAR CONCERTS FROM THE PAYMENT OF AMUSEMENT TAX ON GROSS RECEIPTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PARAGRAPH (c), SECTION 140 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Rationale: The author of this bill explains: It is our position that, Local Government Code's (RA 7160) imposition of an amusement tax on thirty percent (30%) of the gross receipts from admission fees to pop, rock and similar concerts is counter tothis constitutional mandate. Paragraph (c) of Section 140 of the said law states that, "The holding of operas, concerts, dramas, recitals, painting and art exhibitions, flower shows, musical programs, literary and oratorical presentations, except pop, rock, or similar concerts shall be exempt from the payment of the tax herein imposed." It is to be noted that "pop, rock, or similar concerts" are not exempt from the payment of the amusement tax. The imposition of the said tax to these live concerrnts discourahes the organizers and the artists from holding concerts in various venues nationeide in the effort to promote Filipino talents, culture and values.

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE CONFERMENT OF MASTERAL AND DOCTORATE DEGREES AS EQUIVALENT TO FIRST GRADE AND SECOND GRADE CIVIL SERVICE ELIGIBILITY, RESPECTIVELY
rows.abstract: Rationale: By virtues of Republic Act No. 1080, the bar examinations and the examinations given by the various boards of examiners of the Government are declared as civil service examinations. Hence, those who passed these examinations may be appointed into the civil service without the necessity of passing the civil service examinations, except those positions requiring highly specialized knowledge not covered by the ordinary board examinations. > This bill aims to grant the same privilege toholders of masteral and doctorate degrees recognizing their educational competence and fitness for appointment into the civil service by reason of their having completed post graduate studies which, I believe, is equivalant to the passing of the baror board examinations.
